{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOV5s7_c8AAAABix_8dQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bs-hLzhMIpFI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bs-hL", "number": 9, "title": "Add SNES-style save state management and save data profiles for NES and FDS", "body": "## Goal and scope

Bring the current [snes-rust browser demo](https://takahirox.github.io/snes-rust/) save-management experience to nes-rust-neo, for **both ordinary NES cartridges and Famicom Disk System (FDS) games**. Build on the existing unified game picker and shared Rust/Wasm emulator delivered by #3 and #7. A user familiar with the SNES app should recognize essentially the same controls, layout and workflow. Do not introduce separate NES/FDS save-management screens or a manual mode selector.

Use the current SNES implementation as the reference, particularly its [README — Save and resume](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/README.md#save-and-resume), [save profiles and snapshots (#180)](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/180), [unified state selector (#184)](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/184), and [snapshot format and compatibility policy](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/docs/save-states.md). Inspect the reference frontend and storage helpers at a recorded revision; reuse or adapt applicable code and patterns where practical and license-compatible. Do not reproduce obsolete split-button or separate load-history designs.

### Save state UI and behavior

- [ ] Provide one compact shared toolbar group: **Save state ▾ | Save | Load**, styled and positioned like the current SNES app. The selector shows the current target and opens a single scrollable, accessible picker containing **New state** and existing entries with actual emulator screenshots, save timestamps and an obvious selection indicator. Selecting an entry changes only the target, never execution, playback intent or stored data.
- [ ] Save captures the current machine and a corresponding screenshot at a safe emulation boundary. With New state selected it creates and selects a new entry; subsequent saves overwrite that same entry in place and update its timestamp/thumbnail. No additional confirmation or file dialog for ordinary saves. Report success only after persistence succeeds.
- [ ] Load explicitly restores the selected existing state; disable it for New state or when unavailable. Preserve manual Pause, refresh the display to the restored frame, clear stale audio and host input, and resume naturally if the user intended to play. Browsing or dismissing the picker has no effect on gameplay.
- [ ] Provide Remove (with target-specific confirmation), Export and Import state in the same picker, using the SNES reference interaction patterns. Removing the selected state returns selection to New state. Import validates the file and creates a separate entry; never implicitly load or overwrite an existing state. Remember the current target per game/profile during the page session.
- [ ] Keep the existing game picker, playback, CRT/Pixel, scale, audio, fullscreen and touch-controller UX. Hide or disable inapplicable save controls when no game is loaded. FDS retains its existing conditional disk controls; refresh them on state restoration. Keep the interface compact on desktop and mobile portrait/landscape, without separate settings pages.

### Game-native save data profiles

- [ ] Add a separate **Save data** selector near game identity, matching SNES UI and terminology, for battery-backed NES cartridges and writable FDS media. Support multiple independent profiles: ordinary Save 1, New save (fresh native progress), Duplicate current, select/restart using a profile, and Remove with confirmation. A profile with attached states may be removed only after those states have been removed. Non-battery cartridges have one state history per game and do not need a native-save selector.
- [ ] For NES, a profile holds battery-backed PRG RAM; for FDS, it holds the changes to all sides relative to the original image. Fresh FDS saves start from the original disk contents, not an empty/corrupt disk. Profile switching and Reset preserve the appropriate native data and follow the reference's restart semantics. Never write back into the user's original ROM or disk file.
- [ ] Provide Export current save data and Import save data; use raw SRAM with length checks and clear same-ROM guidance, and a versioned identity-checked FDS disk-save/delta format (reuse the existing disk-save representation where suitable). Import creates a separate profile, not an overwrite. Keep state history scoped to game and profile, with media identity using existing NES ROM hashes and FDS canonical side-byte hashes. Headered/headerless copies of the same FDS image share the same identity.
- [ ] Preserve existing remembered games, BIOS and existing native saves. Adopt the existing single native save as the initial normal profile using a small one-time conversion or equivalent safe adoption; do not build a permanent dual-format storage system. Removing a game from the library retains its profiles and states; reimporting the identical media makes them available again.
- [ ] When loading an older state would replace newer game-native data (SRAM or FDS writes), preserve the displaced progress in a visible recovery profile before committing the restoration, following the SNES reference. If a required save, backup or validation fails, do not destructively replace the running machine or previous saved data. Keep recovery understandable and proportionate to ordinary use.

### Rust snapshot and browser persistence

- [ ] Implement a versioned, bounded, integrity-checked snapshot format in the platform-independent Rust core, exposed through the thin Wasm adapter and usable by native tests. Capture all machine data needed for deterministic continuation at a documented safe boundary: CPU/registers/interrupt state, RAM, PPU/framebuffer and timing, APU and DMA, scheduler and bus state, controllers' emulated latch/shift state, and mutable mapper/CHR/PRG RAM state for every currently supported NES board. For FDS also include BIOS identity, adapter RAM, timer/disk IRQs, drive/head/transfer/motor state, inserted/ejected side and in-progress side-change timing, all mutable disk data and FDS expansion audio state. Do not embed immutable ROM or BIOS binaries in exported snapshots.
- [ ] Validate media kind, exact ROM or canonical disk identity, applicable BIOS hash, format version, lengths, integrity and internal state invariants before committing a restore. Bound file and decompression sizes using the supported media limits. Reject wrong media/BIOS, unsupported versions, malformed/truncated or corrupt files safely without modifying the current machine. Use a documented NES-specific state extension (e.g. `.nesstate` for either medium); SNES/Mesen/other emulator formats are not required. Document version compatibility rather than promise all future versions will load old states.
- [ ] Persist state metadata, real screenshots and snapshots locally using IndexedDB or applicable existing storage helpers, with stable entry identity and atomic replacement of an entry's state/thumbnail. Keep history listing efficient without reading every snapshot payload. Reuse browser persistence and operation guards where practical. Native progress and emulator states are distinct concepts. No network transfer, bundled ROMs, BIOS, games or user save data.
- [ ] Update README, Help as needed, and snapshot/profile documentation. Explain backup/export, origin-local storage, compatible media/BIOS/build requirements, profile recovery and browser durability limits.

### Delivery and scope discipline

Follow the pragmatic engineering direction in SNES #180 and #184: prioritize correct normal single-tab usage, actual demonstrated data-loss bugs, safe handling of untrusted files and required CI. Preserve existing simple storage safeguards (including the FDS single-writer lock); do not add speculative cross-tab reconciliation, journals, exhaustive compound-failure matrices, unrelated accuracy changes or UI redesigns. Clearly document unsupported concurrent editing and best-effort browser durability. No autosave-state, rewind, cloud sync or new emulator compatibility work is required.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Deterministic core round trips:** Add and run focused Rust tests that capture, advance with fixed inputs, restore and repeat execution. Compare subsequent CPU/memory state, actual frame hashes and newly generated PCM (not stale host queues) for representative non-battery and battery cartridges, and cover every supported mapper/board's mutable state. Use the existing source-built FDS fixture and BIOS to verify continuation during disk transfer, side changes/ejection, IRQ and expansion audio activity, including writes on multiple sides. Expected: restored hardware state and subsequent outputs match the uninterrupted reference at the documented boundary. Test wrong ROM/disk/BIOS, malformed and truncated input, invalid lengths/versions and corrupted payloads; rejection leaves live state unchanged.
- [ ] **SNES-parity browser UX:** Run real Chromium tests using the actual Wasm build for NES and FDS: select without changing gameplay, save New state, overwrite without increasing count, create another state, restore, remove selected/unselected entries, import/export, cancel, reload and reopen remembered games. Check real captured thumbnails and timestamps, selected target, disabled Load, manual Pause/Play behavior and refreshed FDS side controls. Compare desktop and mobile portrait/landscape screenshots against the recorded SNES reference. Expected: the shared picker and explicit Save/Load actions behave like SNES, without loss of existing game controls or unnecessary NES/FDS UI divergence.
- [ ] **Profiles and progress safety:** Use a battery cartridge and the source-built writable multi-side FDS fixture to create two independent profiles, duplicate, switch/restart, reset, export/import, delete with confirmation and verify profile-specific state histories. Test an existing pre-feature browser save and library entry adopting Save 1, headered/headerless FDS identity, removal/reimport, and reload. Load an older state over newer native progress and verify both restored and recovered bytes, including FDS writes on multiple sides. Simulate ordinary save or recovery write failures: previous state/native progress remains recoverable, failed load does not replace the machine, and an actionable error is displayed. Verify no ROM/BIOS/save traffic and no bundled media. Use local original/audited fixtures only.
- [ ] **Mandatory existing checks:** Run the current README gates: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `node tests/roms/check.mjs`, `node tests/fds/check.mjs`, `cargo build --locked -p nes-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --release`, `npm --prefix web ci`, `npm --prefix web run build`, `npm --prefix web test` (after the documented Chromium installation), `node tests/check-static.mjs` and `git diff --check`. All pass, including existing NES/FDS game, persistence and UI regressions. Required CI on the final revision is green. Update fixture checks if necessary without introducing proprietary test assets.
- [ ] **Documentation and completion:** Record the reference revision, exact focused checks, actual results, screenshot comparisons, snapshot format/limits, supported workflow and material deviations in the PR or linked validation document. Verify README links/commands and storage compatibility policy. No mandatory human confirmation is required. Once required criteria and CI pass and no concrete blocking defect remains, complete review and merge with `Closes #N`; intentionally partial work uses `Related to #N`.

## Post-merge verification

- Verify the Pages deployment after merging to `main` and closing this Issue; record the Actions run and actual public URL (expected https://takahirox.github.io/nes-rust-neo/).
- Smoke-test the published app using locally supplied original test media/BIOS: create, overwrite, load and reopen a state for both NES and FDS; verify profile selection and FDS side restoration, local-only persistence and import/export. Expected: same shared controls, correct restored gameplay, no unexpected console/network errors and no bundled media.
- Record the results in the merged PR or closed Issue. If publication reveals a defect, open a linked follow-up Issue; do not block merge on checks possible only after deployment.
